title: Temporal Dynamics of CO₂ Equilibration Following Ventilator Adjustment: Comparison of Flow-Based (V̇CO₂) and Partial Pressure-Based (PaCO₂ and etCO₂) Markers
summary:
During general anesthesia, breathing is temporarily supported by a mechanical ventilator under the supervision of the attending anesthesiologist. Adjustments to the ventilator settings are routinely made to meet the patient's clinical needs. Such changes alter the body's carbon dioxide (CO₂) levels, but it takes time for the body to reach a new equilibrium. Although several methods are available to monitor these changes, it is not yet well understood how quickly each method reflects the physiological response after a change in ventilation.
The aim of this study is to investigate how different CO₂ monitoring parameters change over time following a standardized adjustment of mechanical ventilation. Adult patients undergoing elective surgery under general anesthesia will be included if an arterial catheter is placed as part of their routine clinical care.
Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two commonly used ventilation strategies that differ in tidal volume. Minute ventilation will then be increased by adjusting the respiratory rate while keeping the tidal volume constant. Over the following 20 minutes, arterial blood samples will be collected at predefined time points, and respiratory parameters recorded continuously by the ventilator, including carbon dioxide elimination and end-tidal carbon dioxide.
Participation does not require any additional invasive procedures, as all blood samples are obtained through the arterial catheter that is already in place for routine clinical care. The results of this study are expected to improve our understanding of how quickly different CO₂ monitoring methods respond to changes in ventilation and may help optimize the interpretation of these measurements in mechanically ventilated patients.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Elective surgery under total intravenous general anesthesia (TIVA)
 -Routine placement of an arterial catheter for perioperative blood gas analysis according to institutional standard operating procedures
- Written informed consent prior to study participatio
Exclusion criteria:
- Inability or refusal to provide written informed consent
- No routine indication for arterial catheter placement during planned procedure
- Clinical contraindications to the standardized ventilatory intervention
(Risk of increased intracranial pressure, Pulmonary hypertension, Refractory, hemodynamic instability, Pregnancy, Requirement for one-lung ventilation)
